requests.change: In clearAll() ("Delete everything on this device"), also delete the kept photos and PDFs. Add `try { indexedDB.deleteDatabase("kaizenedu.files"); } catch {}` next to localStorage.removeItem. No import is needed, so there is no cycle: blobs.ts imports store.ts. My open connection closes itself on versionchange, so the delete is not blocked. Until this lands, lib/blobs.ts deletes the files only where it is loaded, or on the next app page load after the accounts are gone.

In removeLearner(id), delete that learner's files right away. Before filtering events, collect `s.events.filter((e) => e.profileId === id).flatMap((e) => e.attachment?.blobId ? [e.attachment.blobId] : [])`, then after update() call `void deleteBlob(f)` for each (import { deleteBlob } from "./blobs"). Until then, lib/blobs.ts deletes them only on pages where it is loaded, or at the next prune (1-hour grace).

Add an `allowDelete?: boolean` prop (default true) that hides the Delete / "Yes, delete" control. Once it exists, change components/school/SchoolItem.tsx (intake package) in two places: pass `allowDelete={unlocked}` to <EventForm>, and have the Edit button call openEditor() directly instead of `setGate("edit")`. Learners could then edit an item without the grown-up gate, and deleting would stay gated. Also consider gating the calendar page's own Delete the same way: today a child can delete an item there without the gate.

Give the tutor an item's pasted text as well as its notes, capped to the context schema's 1000 characters: `const homework = event ? { title: event.title, notes: [event.notes, event.attachment?.text].filter(Boolean).join("\n\n").slice(0, 1000) || undefined } : ...`. If the tutor route doesn't already strip learner names from notes, run them through lib/intake.ts redactNames first, as the box does.

Sets started from the item page open with ?from=event:<eventId>. Map that back: `exitHref = from === "today" ? "/home" : from?.startsWith("event:") ? `/calendar/${from.slice(6)}` : "/practice"`. Label the finish-screen link with t("intake.backToItem") ("Back to the school item"; the key exists in en and es).

Pre-fill the search from the URL: `const [query, setQuery] = useState(() => params.get("q")?.slice(0, 120) ?? "")`. The box sends /practice?q=<topic>&subject=<subject> (lib/intake.ts practiceSearchHref). Its copy currently promises only "the practice list", so it stays honest until this lands.

Link each school item (week rows, Coming up rows, the plan's due and prep lines) to its page: <Link href={`/calendar/${event.id}`}>. Today the item page can only be reached right after saving from the box.

The h2 above the non-K-2 box, t("today.learnNew") ("Learn something new"), no longer describes it: the box takes homework, tests, practice and learning, and has its own label "What's going on?". Drop that heading, keep the section, and use aria-label={t("intake.label")}, or add a home.* key that covers all four. Optional: pass mode="intake" to both <MagicBox learner={learner} /> calls; it is already the default.

The box now runs the safety screen as you type, so its false positives show up. In CRISIS, `want(ed)? to die` has no closing word boundary, so it matches "want to diet". `end (my|it all)` matches "how do I end my essay". Both show the 988 reply and leave a crisis note for the parents. Suggested: `want(ed)? to die\b` and `end (my life|it all)\b`. Tutor behaviour is otherwise unchanged.
Optional: pass mode="course" explicitly to <MagicBox variant="page" ... />. It is already the default for variant="page", so nothing breaks without it.
